questions.question_text:
Two brands of battery are tested.
The lives, in hours, of five batteries of each brand are:
Brand P: $26$, $27$, $28$, $30$, $34$
Brand Q: $31$, $24$, $29$, $26$, $25$
Using the mean, which brand lasts longer?

options.text: Brand P, mean $29$ h
Brand Q, mean $27$ h
options.why: Calculated both means correctly but chose the smaller one, as if a lower mean meant a longer life.

options.text: Brand P, mean $28$ h
options.why: Found the median of Brand P instead of its mean.

options.text: Brand Q, mean $31$ h
options.why: Used Brand Q's longest single life in place of its mean.

questions.solution_text:
$\overline{x}_{P} = \frac{145}{5}$
$= 29\text{ h}$
$\overline{x}_{Q} = \frac{135}{5}$
$= 27\text{ h}$
Brand P has the higher mean, so Brand P lasts longer.

questions.question_text:
Two sprinters each run $100$ m four times.
Their times, in seconds, are:
Sprinter A: $12.9$, $13.3$, $12.7$, $13.1$
Sprinter B: $13.4$, $12.8$, $13.0$, $13.4$
Using the mean, who is the faster sprinter?

options.text: Sprinter A, mean $13.0$ s
Sprinter B, mean $13.15$ s
options.why: Chose the larger mean, but for a time the smaller mean is the faster result.

options.text: Sprinter B, mean $13.4$ s
options.why: Used Sprinter B's most frequent time (the mode) instead of the mean.

options.text: Sprinter A, mean $12.7$ s
options.why: Quoted Sprinter A's fastest single time rather than the mean of the four times.

questions.solution_text:
$\overline{x}_{A} = \frac{52.0}{4}$
$= 13.0\text{ s}$
$\overline{x}_{B} = \frac{52.6}{4}$
$= 13.15\text{ s}$
Sprinter A has the lower mean time, so Sprinter A is faster.

questions.question_text:
Two machines are tested on five days.
The numbers of items produced are:
Machine M: $88$, $95$, $90$, $93$, $89$
Machine N: $84$, $99$, $91$, $96$, $86$
Using the range, which machine is more consistent?

options.text: Machine M, range $7$
Machine N, range $15$
options.why: Chose the machine with the larger range, but a larger range means the values are more spread out.

options.text: Machine M, range $6$
options.why: Subtracted $95-89$, using Machine M's second-smallest value instead of its smallest.

options.text: Machine N, range $13$
options.why: Subtracted $99-86$, using Machine N's second-smallest value instead of its smallest.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Range}_{M} = 95 - 88$
$= 7$
$\text{Range}_{N} = 99 - 84$
$= 15$
Machine M has the smaller range, so Machine M is more consistent.

questions.question_text:
Two delivery drivers record the times, in minutes, for six deliveries:
Driver G: $21$, $26$, $24$, $30$, $23$, $27$
Driver H: $25$, $22$, $29$, $28$, $24$, $26$
Using the median, which driver is faster?

options.text: Driver G, median $25$ min
Driver H, median $25.5$ min
options.why: Chose the larger median, but for a time the smaller median is the faster result.

options.text: Driver G, median $24$ min
options.why: Took the lower of Driver G's two middle values instead of the mean of the two.

options.text: Driver H, median $26$ min
options.why: Took the higher of Driver H's two middle values instead of the mean of the two.

questions.solution_text:
$21, 23, 24, 26, 27, 30$
$\text{Median}_{G} = \frac{24 + 26}{2}$
$= 25\text{ min}$
$22, 24, 25, 26, 28, 29$
$\text{Median}_{H} = \frac{25 + 26}{2}$
$= 25.5\text{ min}$
Driver G has the lower median time, so Driver G is faster.

questions.question_text:
Two brands of light globe are tested.
The lives, in hours, of six globes of each brand are:
Brand S: $22$, $25$, $25$, $27$, $25$, $29$
Brand T: $24$, $26$, $28$, $30$, $31$, $33$
Which statement about the modes is correct?

options.text: Brand S has mode $25$ h; Brand T has no mode.
Brand S has mode $25$ h; Brand T has mode $24$ h.
options.why: Named Brand T's smallest life as its mode, but no value in Brand T repeats.

options.text: Brand S has mode $25.5$ h; Brand T has no mode.
options.why: Gave Brand S's mean instead of its most frequent value.

options.text: Brand S has mode $25$ h; Brand T has mode $33$ h.
options.why: Named Brand T's longest life as its mode, but no value in Brand T repeats.

questions.solution_text:
$22, 25, 25, 25, 27, 29$
$\text{Mode}_{S} = 25\text{ h}$
$24, 26, 28, 30, 31, 33$
Every value of Brand T occurs once, so Brand T has no mode.

questions.question_text:
The table shows the mean and the range of the numbers of items produced per day by two machines.
$\begin{array}{lcc}\textbf{Machine}&\textbf{Mean}&\textbf{Range}\\ \hline \text{P}&62&18\\ \text{Q}&58&9\end{array}$
Which statement is correct?

options.text: Machine Q is more consistent, because its range is smaller.
Machine P is more consistent, because its mean is higher.
options.why: Judges consistency from the mean, but consistency is shown by the spread, which is the range.

options.text: Machine P is more consistent, because its range is larger.
options.why: Treats a larger range as showing more consistency, but a larger range means the values are more spread out.

options.text: Machine Q produces more per day, because its mean is lower.
options.why: Reads a lower mean as producing more, but a lower mean output means less on average.

questions.solution_text:
$9 < 18$
Machine Q has the smaller range, so Machine Q is more consistent.

questions.question_text:
Two brands of battery are tested.
The lives, in hours, of four batteries of each brand are:
Brand X: $22$, $32$, $27$, $27$
Brand Y: $37$, $17$, $32$, $22$
Using the range, which brand is more consistent?

options.text: Brand X, range $10$ h
Brand Y, range $20$ h
options.why: Chose the brand with the larger range, but a larger range means the values are more spread out.

options.text: Brand X, range $5$ h
options.why: Subtracted $32-27$, using Brand X's second-smallest value instead of its smallest.

options.text: Brand Y, range $15$ h
options.why: Subtracted $37-22$, using Brand Y's second-smallest value instead of its smallest.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Range}_{X} = 32 - 22$
$= 10\text{ h}$
$\text{Range}_{Y} = 37 - 17$
$= 20\text{ h}$
Brand X has the smaller range, so Brand X is more consistent.

questions.question_text:
Two machines are tested over six hours.
The numbers of items made in each hour are:
Machine M: $12$, $22$, $17$, $27$, $22$, $32$
Machine N: $27$, $22$, $32$, $17$, $27$, $22$
Which statement about their means and ranges is correct?

options.text: Machine N has the higher mean ($24.5$) and the smaller range ($15$).
Machine M has the higher mean ($24.5$) and the smaller range ($15$).
options.why: Attached both of Machine N's statistics to Machine M.

options.text: Machine N has the higher mean ($24.5$) and the larger range ($20$).
options.why: Matched each range to the wrong machine.

options.text: Machine M has the higher mean ($22$) and Machine N the smaller range ($15$).
options.why: Chose the smaller of the two means as the higher one.

questions.solution_text:
$\overline{x}_{M} = \frac{132}{6}$
$= 22$
$\text{Range}_{M} = 32 - 12$
$= 20$
$\overline{x}_{N} = \frac{147}{6}$
$= 24.5$
$\text{Range}_{N} = 32 - 17$
$= 15$
Machine N has the higher mean and the smaller range.

questions.question_text:
Two machines are tested on five days.
The numbers of items produced are:
Machine V: $41$, $43$, $44$, $45$, $67$
Machine W: $42$, $46$, $47$, $48$, $52$
Which statement is correct?

options.text: Machine V has the higher mean ($48$) and Machine W has the higher median ($47$).
Machine V has the higher mean ($48$) and the higher median ($44$).
options.why: Compared the means correctly but assumed the same machine must also have the higher median.

options.text: Machine W has the higher mean ($47$) and the higher median ($47$).
options.why: Chose the smaller of the two means as the higher one.

options.text: Machine V has the higher mean ($48$) and Machine W has the higher median ($48$).
options.why: Read Machine W's median from its fourth value instead of its middle value.

questions.solution_text:
$41, 43, 44, 45, 67$
$\overline{x}_{V} = \frac{240}{5}$
$= 48$
$\text{Median}_{V} = 44$
$42, 46, 47, 48, 52$
$\overline{x}_{W} = \frac{235}{5}$
$= 47$
$\text{Median}_{W} = 47$
Machine V has the higher mean and Machine W has the higher median.

questions.question_text:
Two groups of students do a test.
The marks (out of 10) are as follows.
Group A: $6,7,7,7,8,8,9,9$.
Group B: $2,3,5,7,8,8,9,10$.
Three of the following statements are true and one is false.
Which one is false?

options.text: The mean mark for Group B is $6.5$.
options.why: Selected a true statement when asked for the false one: Group B's mean is $52/8=6.5$.

options.text: The range of marks for Group A is $3$.
options.why: Selected a true statement when asked for the false one: Group A's range is $9-6=3$.

options.text: The median mark is the same for each Group.
options.why: Selected a true statement when asked for the false one: both medians are $(7+8)/2=7.5$.

options.text: The marks in Group A have a greater spread than the marks in Group B.

questions.solution_text: Group B has mean $52/8=6.5$. Group A has range $9-6=3$. Both medians are $(7+8)/2=7.5$. However, Group B has range $10-2=8$, larger than Group A’s, so the false statement is D.
